title: Opposite simplicial sets and subdivision Kan zigzags
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, geometric realization, Kan complexes and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], subdivision and its last-vertex map $\lambda$ of [lem-coef-subdivision-face-poset-calculus] and [lem-coef-subdivision-last-vertex-equivalence], and the functor $E=\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}$ with unit $j:T\to ET$ of [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products]. Define $T^{\mathrm{op}}$ by replacing each simplex operator $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ by $\rho_n\alpha\rho_m$, where $\rho_n(i)=n-i$.
For every $T$ there is a natural involutive isomorphism $\eta_T:\operatorname{Sd}T\cong\operatorname{Sd}(T^{\mathrm{op}})$, sending a flag of nonempty subsets $(S_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq S_k)$ in a simplex of dimension $n$ to $(\rho_nS_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\rho_nS_k)$ in the reversed simplex. The maps $\lambda$ give a natural zigzag of weak homotopy equivalences
$$T\leftarrow\operatorname{Sd}T\xrightarrow{\eta_T}\operatorname{Sd}(T^{\mathrm{op}})\to T^{\mathrm{op}}.$$
There is also a natural homeomorphism $|T^{\mathrm{op}}|\cong|T|$ given on realization representatives by reversing the barycentric coordinates. Thus opposite preserves and reflects weak homotopy equivalences and preserves Kan complexes.
For every Kan complex $T$, the zigzag
$$T\xrightarrow{j_T}ET\xleftarrow{E\lambda_T}E\operatorname{Sd}T\xrightarrow{E(\lambda_{T^{\mathrm{op}}}\eta_T)}E(T^{\mathrm{op}})\xleftarrow{j_{T^{\mathrm{op}}}}T^{\mathrm{op}}$$
has only Kan complexes and weak homotopy equivalences. It is natural in $T$. All arrows commute with the maps induced by finite product projections, and the canonical finite-product comparison for $E$ is an isomorphism; no finite-product preservation by $\operatorname{Sd}$ is asserted.
For maps of Kan complexes $u:U\to W$, $v:V\to W$, define $P(u,v)$ by the path-space formula $U\times_{W,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,W)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,W}V$. Reversing the interval and exchanging the two endpoints gives a natural isomorphism $P(u,v)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong P(v^{\mathrm{op}},u^{\mathrm{op}})$, compatible with the constant-path comparisons of strictly commuting squares.

proof.text: Write $\bar\alpha=\rho_n\alpha\rho_m$ for $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$. Reversing both orders makes $\bar\alpha$ monotone; $\overline{\alpha\beta}=\bar\alpha\bar\beta$, $\overline{1}=1$ and $\bar{\bar\alpha}=\alpha$. Thus $T^{\mathrm{op}}(\alpha)=T(\bar\alpha)$ defines an involutive functor, acting on maps by the same degreewise functions. Define $r_n:\Delta^n\to(\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}$ on $m$-simplices by $\gamma\mapsto\rho_n\gamma\rho_m$. For $\beta:[l]\to[m]$, $r_n(\gamma\beta)=(\rho_n\gamma\rho_m)\bar\beta$, proving it is simplicial. The same formula gives its inverse after applying opposite. The image of $\gamma$ omits vertex $a$ precisely when its reversed image omits $n-a$. By the horn description of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], $r_n$ restricts to $\Lambda_i^n\cong(\Lambda_{n-i}^n)^{\mathrm{op}}$.

proof.text: Use the degreewise colimit presentation of $\operatorname{Sd}$ in [lem-coef-subdivision-face-poset-calculus]. On the summand labelled by $t\in T_n$ send a flag $(S_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq S_k)$ to $(\rho_nS_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\rho_nS_k)$ in the summand labelled by the same underlying $t\in(T^{\mathrm{op}})_n$. Images remain nonempty and retain inclusion. If $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ labels a simplex-category relation, its opposite relation is labelled by $\bar\alpha$ since $T^{\mathrm{op}}(\bar\alpha)t=T(\alpha)t$. The equality $\rho_n\alpha(S)=\bar\alpha(\rho_mS)$ proves that the proposed maps respect this relation, hence descend to the colimit. Faces delete flag terms and degeneracies repeat them, so these maps are simplicial. Applying the construction twice fixes every subset and label, proving $\eta_{T^{\mathrm{op}}}\eta_T=1$. A map $f:T\to T'$ only replaces $t$ by $f(t)$, proving naturality.

source.place: Paragraph 2, supporting simplicial enhancement of the derived coefficient adjunction; explicit agent argument for opposite mapping-space comparison, extracted via lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence, step 7.

proof.text: The two maps $\lambda_T$ and $\lambda_{T^{\mathrm{op}}}$ are weak homotopy equivalences by [lem-coef-subdivision-last-vertex-equivalence], which applies to every small simplicial set, with no Kan hypothesis. The middle arrow $\eta_T$ is a simplicial isomorphism by Step 2. Its realization has inverse the realization of its simplicial inverse, so induces inverse functions on components and inverse maps on based homotopy groups by the definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. It is therefore a weak homotopy equivalence. Naturality of $\lambda$ is part of [lem-coef-subdivision-face-poset-calculus]. These give the first claimed natural zigzag.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.4.8, applied at T and its opposite; the middle isomorphism is the explicit construction in Step 2. Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag; read online, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $R_n(t)_i=t_{n-i}$ on $|\Delta^n|$. Define $H_T:|T^{\mathrm{op}}|\to|T|$ by $[u,t]\mapsto[u,R_n(t)]$. For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, the coordinate-sum formula in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] gives $R_n|\alpha|=|\bar\alpha|R_m$: the $j$th coordinate of both is $\sum_{\alpha(i)=n-j}t_i$. Thus the two representatives $(T^{\mathrm{op}}(\alpha)u,t)$ and $(u,|\alpha|t)$ have images identified by the realization relation for $\bar\alpha$. Each map on $T_n\times|\Delta^n|$ is continuous, so the quotient topology gives a continuous descended map. The same construction with $T^{\mathrm{op}}$ gives its inverse since $R_n^2=1$ and opposite is involutive. It is natural since a simplicial map changes $u$ and leaves $t$ unchanged.

proof.text: For $f:A\to B$, Step 4 gives $H_B|f^{\mathrm{op}}|=|f|H_A$. Postcomposition by homeomorphisms has inverse induced by their continuous inverses, on both components and all based homotopy groups. Consequently $f^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence exactly when $f$ is, by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. If $T$ is Kan, apply opposite to a horn map $\Lambda_i^n\to T^{\mathrm{op}}$ and use the isomorphisms of Step 1 to obtain $\Lambda_{n-i}^n\to T$. Fill this horn in $T$, apply opposite to its filler, and precompose with $r_n$ to obtain a filler of the original horn. Its restriction is the original horn map because both reversal formulas square to the identity. This includes $i=0,n$ and $n=1$. Thus $T^{\mathrm{op}}$ is Kan.

proof.text: Put $E=\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}$. By [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products], $EA$ is Kan and $j_A:A\to EA$ is a natural weak homotopy equivalence for every $A$. For a weak homotopy equivalence $f:A\to B$, naturality gives $(Ef)j_A=j_Bf$. In the model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core], weak equivalences satisfy the model-category two-out-of-three axiom. Hence $j_Bf$ is a weak equivalence, and cancellation of the weak equivalence $j_A$ shows $Ef$ is a weak equivalence. This uses no Kan hypothesis on $A$ or $B$, in particular it applies to $A=\operatorname{Sd}T$.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.6.8: the natural-unit square and two-out-of-three; Propositions 3.3.6.7 and 3.3.6.9 supply the unit and Kan assertions. Read online; archive WANTED.

proof.text: Apply Step 6 to $\lambda_T$ and to $\lambda_{T^{\mathrm{op}}}\eta_T$, which are weak equivalences by Step 3 and closure under composition in the model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. The resulting arrows are exactly $E\lambda_T$ and $E(\lambda_{T^{\mathrm{op}}}\eta_T)$. The other two arrows are $j_T$ and $j_{T^{\mathrm{op}}}$. All three middle objects are Kan by [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products]; the two end objects are Kan by hypothesis and Step 5. This proves the displayed all-Kan zigzag. For every $f:T\to T'$, naturality of $j,\lambda,\eta$ and functoriality of $E$ make each of its four squares commute. Take $f$ to be each projection $\prod_aT_a\to T_b$; opposite acts coordinatewise, so its product projection is the opposite projection. These are the required projection squares. Finally [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products] gives the canonical comparison $E(\prod_aT_a)\to\prod_aET_a$ as an isomorphism for finite families, including the empty family, with the stated projection equations. Only the induced maps $\operatorname{Sd}(\operatorname{pr}_b)$ were used.

proof.text: We spell out interval reversal on the path data, using the internal functor definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For an $n$-simplex $h:\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to W$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,W)$, let $R(h):\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to W^{\mathrm{op}}$ be $h^{\mathrm{op}}(r_1\times r_n)$, identifying the opposite of a degreewise product with the product of opposites. Explicitly its value on $(\beta,\gamma)$ in degree $m$ is $h_m(\rho_1\beta\rho_m,\rho_n\gamma\rho_m)$. This is a simplicial map: restricting by $\alpha:[l]\to[m]$ in the target $W^{\mathrm{op}}$ restricts $h$ by $\bar\alpha$, while $\overline{\beta\alpha}=\bar\beta\bar\alpha$ and $\overline{\gamma\alpha}=\bar\gamma\bar\alpha$. For a parameter operator $a:[k]\to[n]$, the opposite functor-space operator sends $h$ to $h(1\times\bar a)$. The identity $\overline{a\gamma}=\bar a\bar\gamma$ shows that applying $R$ to this equals $R(h)(1\times a)$. Thus $R$ is a simplicial map from $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,W)^{\mathrm{op}}$ to $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,W^{\mathrm{op}})$. Double reversal fixes every $(\beta,\gamma)$, so it is an isomorphism. Its restrictions at $0,1$ are respectively the original restrictions at $1,0$, viewed in $W^{\mathrm{op}}$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, supporting simplicial enhancement of the derived coefficient adjunction; explicit agent argument for opposite mapping-space comparison, extracted via lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence, step 7.

proof.text: An $n$-simplex of $P(u,v)^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a triple $(x,h,y)$ with $h|_0=u(x)$ and $h|_1=v(y)$. Send it to $(y,R(h),x)$. Step 8 gives $R(h)|_0=v^{\mathrm{op}}(y)$ and $R(h)|_1=u^{\mathrm{op}}(x)$, so this is an $n$-simplex of $P(v^{\mathrm{op}},u^{\mathrm{op}})$. The outer coordinates restrict by the opposite operators, and the middle one does so by Step 8, proving the map is simplicial. Applying it a second time is the identity, so it is an isomorphism. Postcomposition of $h$ and application of maps to $x,y$ commute with the formula, proving naturality in the entire cospan. For a strictly commuting square with maps $a:Z\to U$, $b:Z\to V$, its constant-path comparison sends $z$ to $(a(z),c_{ua(z)},b(z))$. A constant path at an $n$-simplex $w$ has value $W(\gamma)w$ on $(\beta,\gamma)$. Its reversed value is $W(\bar\gamma)w=W^{\mathrm{op}}(\gamma)w$, independent of $\beta$. Thus reversal sends that triple to $(b(z),c_{v^{\mathrm{op}}b(z)},a(z))$, exactly the constant-path comparison for the exchanged opposite square. Degreewise products and pullbacks are those of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].
